items.title: DeepSeek deep-sixed at all US federal civilian agencies
items.excerpt: DHS on Monday ordered federal civilian agencies to stop using and remove all DeepSeek and DeepSeek-affiliate products, including third-party services developed using DeepSeek; the order's scope is broad and vague. (Yonhap reports China called it politicisation of science and technology.)

items.title: UK finance watchdog wants firms to report AI failures and close calls
items.excerpt: FCA chief data officer Jessica Rusu said firms' incident reporting must cover significant AI failures and near-misses as increasingly autonomous agents enter financial services, demanding clear accountability. (Primary: FCA speech 'Building the future of finance in the age of AI'.)

items.title: Meta tries to scapegoat staff who downloaded torrents to spare execs
items.excerpt: In the authors' AI-training copyright case, Meta was ordered to identify the executives who approved torrenting shadow-library books for AI training; Meta argues nobody 'decided' to pirate books.

items.title: Meta drops the word "train" from its commercial TOS after AI backlash
items.excerpt: Meta changed its commercial terms on AI scraping/training after backlash but won't add language committing to respect robots.txt.

items.title: Democrats warn tech firms of election security 'backsliding' ahead of midterms
items.excerpt: Senior congressional Democrats on intelligence and election oversight sent a letter to 25 companies including Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and TikTok, warning that inaccurate AI-generated voting information and weakened safeguards could expose voters to manipulation before Nov 3.

items.title: Democrats think cracking down on AI could give them an edge
items.excerpt: Democrats are positioning themselves as a regulatory force over the AI industry should they win back control of Congress in the midterms.

items.title: The AI attack-ad nightmare is coming true
items.excerpt: Axios analysis of undisclosed AI-generated midterm attack ads (Georgia, Michigan, New York races); four states ban certain deepfake political ads, 27 require disclosure, no federal law. NOTE: overlaps Wesleyan $137M data already published 10-19.

items.title: AI takes on great experiment in self-rule
items.excerpt: With Washington hands-off and Trump blessing a voluntary framework, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Meta and Nvidia are building self-governance structures and competing wealth-sharing plans. Analysis.

items.title: French Government Calls Emergency Meetings With Platforms Over Protests
items.excerpt: France told TikTok and other platforms to curb protest footage and AI-altered images amid unrest; resale sites reportedly agreed to stop looted goods. AI is a partial hook.

items.title: NYC proposes crackdown on AI customer service chatbots
items.excerpt: Mamdani administration proposed a first-of-its-kind city rule requiring businesses to give customers a quick off-ramp to a human agent when an AI chatbot can't resolve their request. (Off-list; no allowed outlet covered it.)

items.title: S. Korea's U.N. envoy named co-chair of global AI governance dialogue
items.excerpt: UNGA President appointed Korean Ambassador Cha Ji-hoon and Saint Kitts and Nevis' Mutryce Agatha Williams to co-chair preparations for the 2027 UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance (May 3-4, 2027).

items.title: 日, 데이터센터·클라우드 안전인증제 신설…"중국계 배제 목적"
items.excerpt: 일본 정부가 데이터센터·클라우드 안전성 인증 제도를 신설해 중요 개인정보를 다루는 기업이 인증 사업자를 쓰도록 할 방침이며, 사실상 중국계 사업자 배제 목적이라고 닛케이가 보도.

items.title: 백악관 SIF 공동의장 "정부에 협조 않는 AI 기업 제어할 것"
items.excerpt: 백악관 슈퍼인텔리전스 포스(SIF) 공동의장 에밀 마이클 국방부 차관이 정부에 협조하지 않는 AI 기업에 수출통제·외국인 사용 제한 등 행정수단을 동원하겠다고 밝히고, 중국 오픈모델 대응으로 모델 가중치 감사를 언급.

items.title: Investment summit: German government strikes AI deal with Nvidia
items.excerpt: At the 'Invest in Germany' summit in Berlin, the federal government secured a partnership with Nvidia on AI plus new Amazon investment, after Jensen Huang warned Germany is falling behind. Sovereign-AI angle; borderline compute deal.

items.title: GAO to monitor government AI use, hire AI experts in coming years
items.excerpt: GAO's 2027-2032 strategic plan sets goals on overseeing federal AI use and hiring AI experts. (Off-list.)

items.title: AI Hype Helped Google Dodge an Antitrust Breakup. What Comes Next?
items.excerpt: Barry Lynn and Mihir Kshirsagar discuss what the Google search and ad tech remedies mean for competition and accountability in the AI era. Podcast/analysis.

items.title: Is Europe Ready for Advanced AI? The Growing Debate Over Liability
items.excerpt: Interview with FLI's Risto Uuk and MEP Brando Benifei on renewed calls for EU AI liability rules after agent incidents. Analysis.

items.title: Another Week of Lawsuits Piling Up at OpenAI
items.excerpt: Breakdown of eight state AG complaints and five private suits against OpenAI. Mostly follow-up on the 10-15 state lawsuits story.

items.title: Exclusive: The national intelligence chief steering AI
items.excerpt: Profile of the US national intelligence chief's role steering administration AI policy and enforcement. (Off-list.)

items.title: JB Pritzker thinks AI could help us live to 100 — or threaten us like nukes
items.excerpt: Decoder interview: Illinois Gov. Pritzker on state AI laws, privacy, data centers and Congress. Podcast.

items.title: Will developing nations be able to handle millions of AI agents?
items.excerpt: Examines whether Global South regulators and infrastructure are ready for mass consumer AI agents like Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots.

items.title: Cyberattack on French supermarkets tells us more about food security than AI safety
items.excerpt: Opinion/analysis on a cyberattack on French supermarkets and its implications versus AI-safety framing.
